metaTitle: Pallet Standards: ISPM 15, ISO 6780, ASTM D1185, ANSI MH1, and More — AGL Pallet
metaDescription: A guide to the published pallet standards buyers meet: ISPM 15, APHIS rules, ISO pallet standards, ASTM test methods, ANSI MH1, the Uniform Standard for Wood Pallets, and receiver specs, with where to get each.

sections.heading: Kinds of pallet standards
paragraphs: "Pallet standard" can mean several different things. Most fall into one of five groups:
list: Phytosanitary rules: how wood packaging is treated and marked to cross borders. Mandatory where a country enforces them.
Dimensions: principal pallet sizes and tolerances for international handling.
Test methods: how to measure a pallet's strength, stiffness, and durability so results can be compared.
Quality and terminology: minimum lumber and assembly requirements, and a shared vocabulary for specs.
Receiver and pool specifications: requirements set by a retailer, distribution center, or pallet pool for pallets entering its system.
after: Only the first group is law, and only for shipments that cross a border. Domestic pallet standards are voluntary unless a contract or a receiver makes them binding.

sections.heading: Standards buyers meet most
paragraphs: This guide summarizes each standard and links to its publisher. It does not reproduce standard text; buy or download the current edition from the publisher before relying on a clause.

sections.heading: Which standard applies to your load
list: Exporting, or importing into the United States: ISPM 15 treatment and marking, plus any destination-country rules. U.S. imports fall under APHIS regulations. See [heat-treated pallets and ISPM-15](/resources/heat-treated-pallets-ispm-15/).

Shipping into a large retailer or distribution center: the receiver's own pallet specification comes first. Woodpack Global's standards page lists several retailer specifications; some are public and some require a member login.
Shipping on pooled pallets: the pool's specification and rules. See [pooled vs. owned pallets](/resources/pooled-vs-owned-pallets/).
Container programs and international sizes: ISO 6780 principal dimensions. See [pallet sizes](/resources/pallet-sizes/).

Racking, automation, or heavy loads: a performance spec backed by a named test method (ASTM D1185 or ISO 8611) and the support condition. See [pallet weight and load capacity](/resources/pallet-weight-and-load-capacity/).
Everything else: a written spec. Most domestic one-way pallets ship to a spec agreed between buyer and supplier, not to a published standard.

sections.heading: Citing a standard in a spec
list: Name the standard and edition or year, not just the number.
Say which clause or test applies, and the pass criteria, if performance matters.
Where a standard leaves options open, choose them in the spec: dimensions, entry, deck, and fasteners.
Do not rely on grade letters as if they were a standard. Grade names are trade usage and vary by supplier. See [GMA pallets and grades](/resources/gma-pallets-and-grades/).
Ask for evidence that fits the requirement: a treatment stamp for ISPM 15, test data for a rated load, or a sample for a receiver's approval.
after: Mills build to the spec written on the order. Send the standard and the receiver's spec with a quote request so the AGL quote reflects them.

items.question: Is there an official U.S. pallet standard?
answer: Not one that is mandatory for domestic shipping. ANSI MH1 and the Uniform Standard for Wood Pallets are voluntary industry standards, and receivers set their own requirements. The mandatory rules are phytosanitary: wood packaging crossing a border must meet ISPM 15, which APHIS enforces for U.S. imports.

items.question: Is the GMA pallet a standard?
answer: The 48 × 40 inch GMA footprint is a widely followed convention, and 1219 × 1016 mm (48 × 40 in) is one of the principal dimensions in ISO 6780. Grade terms attached to GMA pallets, such as Grade A or Grade B, are trade usage rather than a published standard.

items.question: Where can I get the full text of a pallet standard?
answer: From its publisher. ISPM 15 is a free download from the IPPC, and U.S. regulations are free on eCFR. ISO, ASTM, and ANSI standards are sold by their publishers, and industry and receiver specifications come from the association or receiver that issues them.
